 Nets Notes: Randle, Spirit, MPJ, Demin, Claxton, Wagners
 By Rory Maher |
 at November 20, 2026 6:16 pm 
 Veteran forward Julius Randle called out his Nets teammates for their lackluster performance after Wednesday’s blowout loss to the Bulls, who entered the game with an identical 3-10 record. He also didn’t exempt himself from culpability after finishing with zero rebounds in 26 minutes.
 Randle’s frustration exposed a much bigger problem for Brooklyn, according to C.J. Holmes of The New York Daily News , who says this season’s group has lacked the “competitive spirit” that defined head coach Jordi Fernandez ’s first two years with the Nets. Despite clearly being at a talent deficit, those teams played with a baseline level of effort that has repeatedly been called into question in 2026/27.
 Fernandez expressed his own frustration after Wednesday’s game and said his messaging wasn’t getting through to the players. That raises an “uncomfortable question” about the direction of the team, Holmes writes, given that effort appeared so fundamental to Fernandez’s tenure.
 “ Today we played 48 minutes of meaningless basketball, and it doesn’t matter how much the young guys play, it does not matter at all if those minutes are not played correctly by the whole team ,” Fernandez said Wednesday.
 Everyone involved in the situation holds some responsibility in the team’s poor performance, per Holmes, who believes the club needs to maintain a certain standard otherwise the same talking points will be repeated after additional disappointing losses.
 Here’s more on the Nets:
 Michael Porter Jr. , who had his worst game of the season on Wednesday (five points on 1-of-7 shooting), said Friday that the team held a meeting after Wednesday’s loss, as Brian Lewis of The New York Post reports ( Twitter links ). “ Yeah, there was a lot of internal discussion that I’ll keep between the team, but just realizing we got to be better and addressing what needed to be addressed ,” said Porter, who added that “everybody” contributed to the discussion. “ Everybody. Everybody collectively. I thought it was a good conversation, and everybody pitched into what they saw .” 
 2025 lottery pick Egor Demin , who’s had a rocky start to his second season, took responsibility for his play on the defensive end on Wednesday after the Nets gave up 76 first-half points and 137 overall, Holmes writes for The Daily News . “ Everything was missing. I don’t know. I mean, we got to be better on defense in all aspects and starting with me ,” the Russian guard said. “ So, yeah. ” For what it’s worth, Demin was benched on Friday in favor of Danny Wolf , tweets Holmes.
 Nic Claxton , who spent his first seven years in Brooklyn after being selected 31st overall in 2019, had nothing but good things to say about his former team after Wednesday’s game, per Julia Poe of The Chicago Tribune . The Nets traded Claxton to the Bulls over the summer as part of the Randle deal. “ There’s no ill will at all, ” Claxton said. “ It’s all good vibes. I don’t have anything negative to say about anybody in this organization, in Brooklyn. I’m grateful for my time here. I had a beautiful time here. … It’s all love .”
 Friday’s game between the Magic and Nets will mark the first time brothers Franz Wagner and Moritz Wagner have played against each other professionally, writes Jason Beede of The Orlando Sentinel . Center Moe spent the last five years in Orlando being both a teammate and a roommate with his younger brother before signing a two-year deal with the Nets. “ It’s definitely going to be a little weird ,” Franz explained. “ We’ve obviously played in practice against each other. But I look at it like this, it’s a huge blessing to be able to share the court together at this level. I’m really happy for him in the situation that he’s in. I think me, Moe and the rest of the family will enjoy the game as much as anything .” Moe, who’s known for being an on-court irritant, said he wasn’t sure what to think of the situation, according to Holmes . “ It’s awkward. I’m not going to lie. I don’t really know how to compartmentalize and really deal with it ,” he said before the game. “ I’ll try to focus on the game plan and see what happens emotionally .”

 Front office, head coach, and the vet “stars” all deserve each other here. Marks has had a number of misses in the draft and, frankly, compiled too many young players to give all of them a fair shot at development. Jordi is running some weird rotations and, more specifically, not playing guys more like Mann and Minott who would address the effort issue and surely could do no worse on the court than some of the guys being gifted minutes. Randle and MPJ have had effort and/or temperament questions follow them for years. One is a ball hog and lazy, the other a general sieve defensively. A completely rudderless ship.
 Yes, this was intended to be a stop-gap year, but I would not assume things are going to look significantly better in a year or two.

 BKN isn’t doing anything different on the court than the NBA’s perma-tankers of the last decade. Young guys and misfit vets in musical chair rotations. Three non-playoff years straight, with this looking like a lock to be year 4.
 The difference with BKN is, so far, is that they haven’t been blessed by the ping pong ball Gods. They’ve had only 2 first round picks (above #19) in the past decade. #8 in 2025, and #6 in 2026. They also don’t control their own FRP this coming year, so it’s likely to continue through years 5 and 6. 
 I don’t like tanking, and think it’s an embarrasment to the league and the sport. But in a league that’s rewarded it for over a decade, I can’t blame them for doing it until they get theirs. Fire everyone for being unlucky? It got Moe Greene killed, so maybe that’s how it has to end.
